description: The reader floor: at least one critical schema item over the findings shape, and provenance on every grounded claim. Two todos share one frozen schema. The conforming product passes; the product whose single finding dropped its provenance key fails, and the refusal names the JSON path the schema rejected.
decisions: Provenance is a required property of the findings item, not a separate judge item. A deterministic shape check is what the reader floor can actually enforce before F3a; whether the provenance is honest is the judge's question and is out of scope here.
Both todos name the same schema artifact, so the fixture also pins that two verdicts over one criterion carry the same criteriaDigest.

The schema uses only the supported subset (type, required, properties, items) plus description, which is on the allowed descriptive list. The unsupported-keyword refusal is schema::unsupported_schema_assertion_is_refused, a different test with a different fixture.
The failing verdict's detail names $.findings[0].provenance. A refusal that only says the document is invalid sends the model back to guess, which is how a repair loop turns into a retry loop.
